edges.description: Reproduces particle retention in alveolar macrophages and the inflammatory response, but shows that response to be absent below 500 mg/m3 and transient at that dose, so it does not reproduce the sustained inflammation a chronic fibrotic human disease would require.
edges.limitations: A single acute exposure at 1 to 500 mg/m3 against decades of workplace exposure, and the material was synthetic graphite containing less than 0.1% quartz rather than the mixed natural dust workers inhale. The model therefore informs the pure-graphite question well and the human mixed dust disease poorly. Lavage cell profiles are not fibrosis endpoints.
edges.source: Fischer 344 rat acute graphite versus silica inhalation comparison

nodes.description: Graphite particles are ingested by alveolar macrophages and persist within them for months without killing them, since lavaged cells showed no loss of viability after either graphite or silica exposure. Retention without cytotoxicity is the point at which the graphite and silica pathways diverge.
nodes.id: Alveolar macrophage retention of graphite particles

nodes.description: There is no treatment that reverses pneumoconiosis, so the whole therapeutic content of this disease is preventing further deposition. Dust control in one mine was followed by a fall in radiographic lesion prevalence across successive surveys.

nodes.description: Breathlessness is the main symptom of established disease. In the index case of the historical literature it appeared eight years after the man had left the graphite mill, which is the latency this disease is known for.

evidence.snippet: Eight years after leaving the graphite mill he lost weight and developed marked dyspnea.

nodes.description: Fischer 344 rats given a single acute inhalation exposure to synthetic graphite at 1 to 500 mg/m3, or to silica at 100 mg/m3 as a within-experiment comparator, with bronchopulmonary lavage cells followed for about three months. This is the controlled comparison that separates the effect of graphite from that of silica, which no human cohort does.

nodes.description: Human disease shows peribronchiolar dust macules, reticular and nodular change and, in a subset, confluent fibrosis, with lavage and biopsy consistent with mixed dust pneumoconiosis. The lesion is real and reproducible across cases; what is unresolved is how much of it graphite itself produces.

nodes.description: Occupational aerosolization in mines, mills, foundries and electrode manufacture delivers respirable graphite-containing dust to the small airways and alveolar regions. The inhaled material is not pure graphite, because natural graphite carries quartz and other minerals, which is why the disease is conventionally called a mixed dust pneumoconiosis.

nodes.description: Graphite produced inflammation and macrophage activation only at the highest dose tested and only for about 24 to 48 hours. Below 500 mg/m3 the inflammatory changes were absent altogether, whereas silica at 100 mg/m3 produced persistent inflammation and lasting macrophage activation. The inflammatory response to nearly pure graphite is therefore weak and self-limited in this experiment.
